notes.claim: A vector has both a magnitude and a direction, and velocity, force and acceleration are physical quantities it can represent.
Vector quantities cannot be added, subtracted, multiplied or divided by simply adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing their magnitudes.

sources.title: Vectors: FAQ (article) | Vectors | Khan Academy
sources.quote: A vector is a mathematical object that has both a magnitude (length) and a direction. Vectors can be used to represent physical quantities such as velocity, force, and acceleration.

sources.title: 16.1: Vectors - Engineering LibreTexts
sources.quote: In contrast with scalar quantities, we cannot add, subtract, multiply or divide them by simply adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing the magnitudes.
